questions: When swapping A_i and A_j, must i and j be distinct positions? (If the same position is chosen, the swap does nothing; is that allowed as an operation?)

Does the operation allow swapping any two positions where one holds value a and the other holds value b, even if those positions are not currently occupied by the same couple? (i.e., can we swap an 'a' with a 'b' regardless of where they are?)

Must the swaps be performed only among the four people (two a's and two b's), or can other values be moved indirectly via swapping a and b? (The operation only swaps a and b directly, but could that affect positions of other values?)

Is the goal to have both couples adjacent simultaneously in the final state, or is it sufficient that each couple could be made adjacent in separate states? (The condition says 'reach a state where the two occurrences of a in A are adjacent and the two occurrences of b in A are also adjacent.')
Are we allowed to perform swaps involving other couples (c, d, etc.) during the process, or only swaps between a and b? (The operation definition only mentions swapping a and b.)
Does 'adjacent' mean immediately next to each other in the sequence (i.e., positions k and k+1)?

If the two occurrences of a are already adjacent, is the pair (a,b) automatically disqualified even if b's occurrences are not adjacent and swaps could make b adjacent? (The first condition requires a's occurrences not adjacent.)
Is the sequence A modified in place for each test case independently, or are we considering the original A for all conditions? (The operation is hypothetical; we are not actually modifying A.)
